svg.text: NC current-state operating model — dependencies from the engineer’s workspace out
Innermost layer = vCloud Director. Every ring outside it is something that workspace sits on. Shapes follow Lucidchart conventions.

How to read this. The engineer only works in the centre. Each ring around that centre is a dependency — take a ring away and the ring inside it stops working. Access comes in from the left, through the jump server. Ownership is labelled on the right of each ring.
OUTER RING · physical kit and the access path
Nothing in the inner rings exists without this. Invisible to the engineer.
No direct path from laptop to vCenter.
Physical machines this ring is made of
MIDDLE RING · platform the portal sits on
vCloud Director cannot place a VM unless these four things answer the request.
picks a host · manages VM lifecycle

The operating model in one sentence
The engineer is self-service inside a fence.
Everything the fence sits on is TechOps.
vCloud Director is the only shared surface.
Lucidchart shape map — rebuild with these exact shapes
Rounded process — interface (VPN, vCloud Director portal)
Process — named product (vCenter, ESXi, AlgoSec, Palo Alto)
Data store / cylinder — any machine or array (jump server, SAN, blades, switches)
Terminator / pill — owner label (Engineer or TechOps)
Decision — workshop question on the fence
Dashed process — reconstructed, not confirmed for NC

Assumption sitting outside the rings: this stack is rebuilt from the Mannheim Network Control Service pattern (about 10–15 jump servers) under a vCloud Director portal used across the software factory. If NC’s real setup differs, the rings still hold. The product names on the dashed boxes may not.
